findings.reason: the required change (resolve format/root from the catalogue and retire the probe-angle machine branch) is unchanged; only the description of the starting point is imprecise.
findings.text: §4 calls `read_geometry_table` an extension point that "today resolves one fixed store format and root", but `store_format` and `store_root` are already keyword parameters (defaults `"zarr"` and `LEVEL2_DIR`); the only machine-name branch is `_supply_declared_probe_angles` at line 103, so the section overstates the store work and understates that only the probe-angle branch is machine-named

findings.reason: without naming where the JT-60SA semantic identity is registered and by which function it is authored from the §4 netCDF, §7's spine gate has no executable artifact source and risks a second resolver beside the pinned one the plan explicitly rejects.
findings.text: §7 says the spine reads JT-60SA geometry "with a JT-60SA pin rather than a second resolver (so `resolve_machine_description` gains a machine to resolve, and how the artifact is authored from the §4 source ... is settled in this section)", but the section does not settle it: `author_pinned_description` takes no machine and hard-imports `nova.imas.mast_geometry`, `PINNED_SEMANTIC_IDENTITY`/`PINNED_PHYSICAL_DIGEST`/`PINNED_REGISTRY_DIGEST` are single module constants (lines 69–78), and `select_machine`/`resolve_machine_description` take no machine argument, so a JT-60SA pin needs a machine-keyed pin registry and a non-nova authoring entry point that the plan leaves unnamed

findings.reason: one sentence recording that the two store-addressing keys retire nothing (the catalogue had no store-format slot) or merge into the engine's existing `store_format` concept would satisfy the interface-budget rule the other sections already meet.
findings.text: §4 grows `load_machine_map`'s "fixed key set" by three catalogue entries under its own "§2 slot rule" (justified-by-structure), but states a retirement only for the probe-angle source / machine branch; the description store-format and store-root keys add public map-schema surface with no statement of what they retire or merge or why nothing can, unlike §2, §3 and §7 which each carry that sentence

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new pieces hide substantial behaviour behind small interfaces: one batch-fetch function plus one cache writer at the ssh boundary; one exporter function; one EQDB remote script riding the §3 transport. No spread of shallow wrappers over the same machinery.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the artifact-identity owner in `gs/artifact_resolution.py` is extended for resolution, but its pin store is a single module-level constant and its authoring route is MAST-only through nova, so "a JT-60SA pin of its own" names no mechanism.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — §4 adds catalogue keys (store format, store root, probe-angle source) to the public map schema and names a retirement only for the probe-angle machine branch, leaving the store-format and store-root keys as added public-definition surface with no retire, merge or why-nothing statement.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — every proposed mechanism is placed against a named existing owner (paths.py, transform_engine.py, description_reader.py, cocos_convention.py, efit_referee.py, artifact_resolution.py), and each cited symbol exists, though §4's account of `read_geometry_table` is imprecise (below).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the remote extractor is the only wrapper risk and §3 states why codex's layer cannot be imported (graph/LLM/tool-install dependencies on every ambix read) and explicitly defers a shared remote core to the second facility that needs one.
